title: 47F nonsmoker with ongoing dizziness 2 months post Covid 19 diagnosis
selftext: I have been dealing with ongoing dizziness and fatigue since my covid 19 diagnosis in August. I am finally back to work 5 days this past week, but I work in rehab in a nursing home and have to be on my feet a lot, so my orthostatic symptoms are very inconvenient. I had one chest xray that showed mild interstitial prominence/lung inflammation while experiencing chest pain in week 4. All my blood work (x3) has been in the normal range since my diagnosis. I am mostly now just having orthostatic symptoms and fatigue. My doctor ordered a holter monitor 2 weeks ago for me and has never communicated the results to me. I can see looking at the result in my chart online that she wrote: "Interpretation: sinus, rare PACs" next to the entry for Holter monitor. I don't have any idea what that means. I'm assuming since she didn't call me that the result is nothing to worry about. I am assuming that the reason I am having orthostatic symptoms is just because my body took a hit when I got the virus and it hasn't totally recovered yet. \[Here's an example of my blood pressures this morning taken with my CVSHealth auto BP cuff: Lying down: 93/52 pulse 52; Standing: 82/62 pulse 119\] Can you tell by my doctor's note on the Holter monitor if there is anything going on heart-wise that I should inquire about? Maybe I am just deconditioned from lying around during my period of fatigue and I should start pushing myself to do more exercise? Any feedback/direction would be helpful. Thank you.

title: Father (64) is able bodied but is bedridden 24/7 peeing in diapers. Can I contact his PCP?
selftext:
My father is 64. 5"11' 180lbs several medications. I'm sorry I don't know them. Some for depression. Former heavy smoker for 45 years. Now rarely smokes. Only when he goes outside and he doesn't. Has a traumatic brain injury from 1984. Prostate issues that cause some leakage and the usage of diapers.

My dad is 64 and has no motivation to do anything anymore.

He used to be a heavy smoker and as bad as it sounds at least he used to go out and smoke several times a day and spend time outside with the dog. Well over the winter he stopped going outside because it was too cold (never stopped him the past 45 years) and he never started again. My dad has zero social life. He lays in his room and watches television. He doesn't go to the store ever or out to eat or anything. He gets a haircut every month and that's about it.

Well recently he developed a problem with his prostate. He had some leakage that got to be a bit of a problem and needed to start wearing diapers while hopefully Flomax kicked in in 2-6 weeks to help him control this leakage.

From the first day he got his diapers he no longer even attempted to get up to pee again even though he still has significant bladder control and his issue is just post-urination dribble. He now just lays in bed and pees in his diapers all day and watches television. He's too lazy to even get up and pee now. He used to mow the lawn. My mother hired a service last month because he complained of his prostate issue. I can see that but I highly doubt he will ever do yardwork again. He's content just laying there.

When we confront him he lies to us like a child (brain injury) He's unaware that my mother who lives with him is able to notice he hasn't once gotten up to pee in over a week and the amount of diapers he's burning through is significant.

My mother drew the line when he requested that she take his bag of diapers out to the alley for him like he was bedridden or something.

He has a nice relationship with my sister's 1 year old but now him and his room reek of urine so she doesn't want him around him anymore and tomorrow is father's day.

I attend his psychiatry sessions with him and they're absolute garbage. He just says he's doing good and then they talk about the 1970s for 15 minutes because they're both old men. I could certainly bring up the diaper thing next time because this is more recent.

He stopped therapy in March. I did not attend those sessions with him.

Can my mother or I contact his PCP about this? Or would that be breaking some doctor/patient confidentiality?

I know you may recommend nursing homes but then my question goes to.... While he already has medicare, How does the nursing home get funded while keeping my mother in the house since his social security disability is more than half of their income....? Probably wouldn't work. She needs to bite the bullet and care for him, no?

Thanks so much!

Edit: I should mention he just saw his PCP in May. But he did not share his results so we have no idea what they found. Maybe a thyroid issue? He wasn't put on any medication we know for sure so I guess that would rule that out, no?

title: How to protect mouth, throat, and nose when sleeping in subfreezing temperatures?
selftext:
36; male; 6’; 180lbs; occasional smoker; no medical issues; no medications; duration is 2 years; location is mouth, throat, and nose


Like a lot of people, I am currently homeless and living in my vehicle. I’ve made it through the last two winters but there were occasions where I think the cold dry air really messed me up.

I have a proper sleeping bag, so my body temperature has been OK, but even if I cover my face while I’m sleeping, inevitably, I’ll uncover it while I’m asleep to breathe easier and I’m afraid that I run the risk of getting really sick.

Obviously, the real answer is sleeping in a suitable environment, but short of that what would you recommend to prevent winding up in the hospital?

Thanks for your help.

title: How do I sober up faster?
selftext: 33m 190 pounds, full blown alcoholic. If my BAC drops I’ll start shaking. 750ml of vodka a day. My job essentially told me they know and I admitted it. However, they think I’m just drinking at night and not at work. I work as a welder in South Florida temperatures in a warehouse with no air conditioning. I’m trying to get off the sauce but I can’t really function through withdrawals. I’ve missed a lot of work and sweating profusely and I was honest with them and said I’m trying to stop but I’d have to take more days off. I was told I had to figure out how to detox and show up for work if I wanted to keep my job. I already know people are gonna tell me to go to the hospital and find another job. I’d like to, but I’d also like to feed my kids and have shelter. I know to taper, but how else can I do this? Vitamins? Exercise? I’m sweating so much at work I had to leave today with heat exhaustion. I threw up for an hour and my muscles are still cramped. 2 pedialytes drank so far and some food in my stomach.
